app.name: NetMaster
app.otherWindowTitle: The app is open in another window
app.otherWindowBody: Two windows writing progress would overwrite each other — so only one window learns at a time. Close the other one, or take over here.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: Your progress is safe on this device. Reloading usually fixes it; if it keeps happening, screenshot this and send it to the app author.
error.rollbackNote: Still broken after reloading? Roll back to the copy the app kept for you. Anything learned after that point is lost, but you get back into the app right away — and the older progress is untouched.
error.rollbackConfirm: Roll progress back to the copy kept at {luc}? The current state is copied first, so a slip can still be undone.
error.noiDungBody: Usually this is a shaky connection. Your progress is still safe on this device — what's missing is only the lesson content, still on its way. Once you're back online, hit Try again; nothing is lost.

feedback.tier3Note: Read the solution, then type the answer yourself — typing it is how it sticks.

after-solution: You read the solution and then typed it out yourself — that second part is where memory forms.
You saw the answer and still came back to do it on your own. That is how a trade is learned.
You had to open the solution here, and you closed it again to do the work. Next time will be lighter.
self-corrected: Wrong once, fixed by yourself, no answer key needed — the most valuable habit in this trade.
You tried again and found it. That stumble is exactly what makes it stick.
You neither gave up nor peeked. That is how someone who fixes real machines works.
hands-lab: You rebuilt it on the diagram instead of just talking theory — networks listen to hands, not words.
You kept fixing until the packet got through: that is the job of someone on network duty.
Try, read the result, fix again. That loop is what this whole trade runs on.
hands-cli: You checked the table with a command before concluding — the habit of someone good at this.
Right command, right column, right fix. That console is the one you meet on the job.
You let the device state its own condition instead of guessing on its behalf.
hands-ps: You asked the system with a command instead of clicking around — this still works at three hundred machines.
One line does what ten minutes of clicking does. You picked the right road.
You verified with a command after the fix instead of trusting a vague "should be done".
hands-palace: You walked the room from memory, no notes. The images are doing the remembering for you.
Remembered as a route through a building, not as a list — that is the whole point of this palace.
The door was closed and you still described the room: it lives in you now.
hands-clinic: You narrowed the fault down before touching anything. That is how a shift engineer works.
You read the signs first and concluded second — every case needs that order.
One case closed. Next time these symptoms show up, your hands will be faster than your head.
retrieval: You recalled it with the lesson closed — that is knowing; recognising it on a reread is not.
No looking back at the page. Every time memory is pulled out, it comes back stronger.
You dug this one out of your own head, and the digging is what makes memory last.
first-try: Right on the first try — this part is solid for you.
Straight out, no hints needed. Your foundation is holding.
Correct from the first attempt. Onwards.
Not a single stumble — what you just learned has stuck.

learn.title: Learn
learn.emptyBody: Part A modules will appear here. Each module follows your letter through the Internet's postal system.
learn.thieuBody: The list below is short because of the connection, not because the course ends there. Keep going as normal through "{ten}" — you won't need the rest until then, and none of your progress is affected.
learn.thieuTuXong: You are back online and the rest has downloaded.
learn.thieuVanChua: Still no luck — the connection looks weak. Try again in a bit.
learn.lessonLocked: Finish the previous lesson to unlock this one
learn.overdueBlockTitle: Your review box needs you first
learn.overdueBlockBody: Overdue backlog: {count}. Clear some of it before starting new lessons — well-timed review is what makes it stick.
learn.drillCardBody: 10 problems a day, against the clock — get fast with the magic number.
learn.challenge: I already know this — test out of it
learn.vmLabNoXp: Real-world work outside the app — it can't be verified, so no XP.
learn.streakFrozen: You skipped a stretch — {used} freeze(s) kept your streak alive ({left} left this month).
learn.streakReset: Your streak restarts today — those {lost} earlier days are still {lost} days you learned; nobody takes that away.
learn.vlsmCardBody: 5 range-carving problems a day — correct, complete, no waste.

today.title: Today
today.partCardsQuen: Review due: {count} — {quen} of them are ones you keep forgetting, and now is exactly when meeting them again makes them stick.
today.quayLai: Good to see you again — your last session was {ngay} days ago. A gap is not a hole: we start again from the review box, gently.
today.fading: {count} cards are fading — not due yet, but they will be soon. Memory cooling on schedule is exactly how this works.
today.conCoTheLuyen: Out of lessons does not mean out of work — two practice grounds stay open, and neither is graded:
today.doneBody: Nothing is due today and you have reached the end of the road so far. Resting is part of remembering — see you tomorrow.

test.title: Module test
test.intro: {count} questions, {threshold}% needed to unlock the next module. No hints mid-test — this is where the knowledge stands on its own. Missing is fine: retake as many times as you like.
test.introFinal: {count} questions, {threshold}% needed to close out the whole course. No hints mid-test — this is where the knowledge stands on its own. Missing is fine: retake as many times as you like.
test.passTitleFinal: {pct}% — you just finished the final module of the course!
test.failBody: You need {threshold}% to unlock the next module. Read through the ideas below, then retake — retakes are for learning, not punishment.
test.failBodyFinal: You need {threshold}% to close out the course. Read through the ideas below, then retake — retakes are for learning, not punishment.
test.failBodyFar: You need {threshold}% to unlock the next module. This one is still a fair way off, so going back to the lessons will be much faster than retaking right now. The test stays open — come back whenever you feel ready.
test.failBodyFarFinal: You need {threshold}% to close out the course. This one is still a fair way off, so going back to the lessons will be much faster than retaking right now. The test stays open — come back whenever you feel ready.
test.reviewHintGeneric: Revisit the lessons that teach these, then retake — full answers appear once you pass.
test.notReadyBody: Finish the lessons in this module first — the test draws on exactly that material.
test.challengeIntro: The same {count} questions as the end-of-module test, {threshold}% needed. Pass and this module counts as done and the next one opens — no sitting through material you already know.
test.challengeOneShot: Not passing costs you nothing: you can test out again straight away, or study it normally and take the end-of-module test like everyone else.
test.challengePass: {pct}% — you tested out, and the next module is unlocked!
test.challengePassFinal: {pct}% — you tested out of the final module, and that closes the whole course!
test.challengePassCards: This module's concepts just went into your review box, due tomorrow. Knowing it today is no promise you will recall it in three weeks — a few minutes of review a day is what keeps it.
test.challengeFailBody: Short of {threshold}%. You can test out again right away, though a couple of lessons from this module first would make it surer.

lesson.pretestIntro: Guess freely — this part is never scored.
lesson.orderHelp: Tap the lines in the order you think is correct.
lesson.selfExplainPassed: You explained it in your own words — that's how it really sticks!
lesson.notFound: This lesson could not be found.
lesson.summaryVisualAlt: Diagram of the network you just built

review.title: Review
review.emptyBody: Finish your first lesson and the first card will schedule itself here — right before your brain lets it slip.
review.noneDueBody: Your cards are still "resting" — come back on {nextDate}. Spacing is the secret to remembering.
review.noneDueBodyNoDate: Your cards are still "resting" — come back later. Spacing is the secret to remembering.
review.selfGradeHint: Grade yourself honestly — cards you miss come back sooner to help you.
review.doneBody: You remembered {correct}/{total} cards. Missed cards return tomorrow.
review.whyHere: Today's session: {count} cards. Your brain is right on schedule to forget, so let's review first.
review.whyHereMore: Another {con} are due as well — those keep for the next session.
review.comeback: You have forgotten this one {count} times before — see how it goes today.
review.confidenceAsk: Before you flip it: how sure do you feel?
review.showAnswerHint: You just saw the answer for this one — this time simply recall it.
review.calibOver: You felt sure about that one but could not recall it — that is the fluency illusion: rereading feels familiar, so it passes for knowing. Let it come back; next time will be different.
review.calibUnder: You said no idea and still recalled it — you are rating yourself lower than you are. Try recalling before deciding you have forgotten.
review.calibDone: Your self-rating matched on {aligned}/{total} cards — knowing what you know is a skill too, and it trains.
review.calibDoneOver: On {count} cards you felt sure but could not recall: those are the ones most worth reviewing.

drill.title: Subnetting drill
drill.intro: 10 freshly generated problems a day, against the clock so your mental math speeds up. Mistakes are fine — the timer is only you racing yourself.
drill.qNetworkAddr: Find the network address of host {ip}/{prefix}.
drill.qBroadcast: Find the broadcast address of host {ip}/{prefix}.
drill.qHostRange: Host {ip}/{prefix}: find the first and last usable host (as "a - b").
drill.qHostCount: How many usable hosts does network {ip}/{prefix} have?
drill.qPrefixForHosts: You need room for {hosts} hosts — what is the smallest sufficient prefix (as /xx)?
drill.qMaskFromPrefix: Convert /{prefix} to a full subnet mask.
drill.qPrefixFromMask: Which prefix does subnet mask {mask} correspond to (as /xx)?
drill.backTomorrow: Come back tomorrow — steady practice is what builds speed.
drill.alreadyDoneToday: You already drilled today. Fancy one more round?

vlsm.title: VLSM design practice
vlsm.intro: 5 fresh problems a day: one address range and a few departments, and you decide how to carve it up. There is no single right answer — any layout counts as long as it is correct, complete and wastes nothing. The timer is only you racing yourself: design takes minutes, and taking your time is normal.
vlsm.brief: You are given the range {base} and must split it between the {count} departments below. Fill in a network address and prefix for each one.
vlsm.criteriaTitle: The three criteria for a design

criteria.correct: Correct: every block sits inside the given range, on a proper boundary, big enough, and never overlaps another
criteria.noWaste: No waste: every block is the smallest size that fits

issue.invalid: the address or prefix cannot be read
issue.outside-base: the block falls outside the given range
issue.not-network-address: this is not the network address of that block
issue.too-small: the block has no room for that many machines
issue.wasteful: the block is larger than needed
issue.overlaps: the block overlaps another department's block

vlsm.solutionTitle: One layout that meets the requirements
vlsm.solutionNote: This is only one option. A different order, or leaving spare room, is accepted too as long as all three criteria hold.

onboarding.invite: Before you learn a single thing — try sending a packet.
onboarding.deliveredBody: Your packet left Machine A, stopped by the router — the "mail carrier" read the address on the envelope and forwarded it — and landed at Machine B. This whole course is the story behind that trip.
onboarding.diagramAria: Network diagram: Machine A connects through a router to Machine B

lab.title: Network lab
lab.goalBlocked: {from} must NOT be able to reach {to}
lab.trayLocked: This task uses exactly the devices already on the bench.
lab.canvasAria: The network diagram you are building
lab.canvasEmpty: The bench is empty — add a device to begin.
lab.panelPick: Pick a device — tap one below, or tap it on the diagram.
lab.portPickTarget: Pick a free port to connect to {port}:
lab.sendFree: Try as many times as you like — this part is never scored.
lab.submitHint: Only submitting counts as an attempt. Experiment first, submit when you're ready.
lab.hopEmpty: Press "Try it" to watch a packet travel through your diagram.
lab.reasonBroadcastFlood: asking the whole network — who holds this address?
lab.reasonUnknownUnicastFlood: the switch doesn't know which port yet, so it sends to all of them
lab.reasonMacTableHit: the switch remembers the destination and sends out exactly one port
lab.reasonRouted: router forwards it — new hardware address, same IP address
lab.resultOk: The packet arrived and a reply came back.
lab.resultReachedOnly: The packet arrived, but there is no way back for the reply.
lab.resultFail: The packet never reached its destination.

failure.src-not-found: The sending machine could not be found.
failure.dst-not-found: The receiving machine could not be found.
failure.src-no-ip: The sender has no IP address yet.
failure.dst-no-ip: The receiver has no IP address yet.
failure.src-no-link: The sender isn't plugged into anything.
failure.no-gateway: The destination is outside the local range and the sender has no way out (gateway).
failure.gateway-off-subnet: The gateway address isn't in the machine's own range, so it can't be reached.
failure.arp-unresolved: The sender asked "who holds this address?" and nobody answered.
failure.no-route: The router has no path towards that address range.
failure.hop-budget-exceeded: The packet kept bouncing between routers without arriving.
failure.broadcast-storm: The network has a loop: the broadcast came back to where it started and multiplied.
failure.trunk-vlan-not-allowed: The frame could not leave the trunk: its VLAN is not on the trunk's allowed list.
failure.native-vlan-mismatch: The two ends of the trunk declare different native VLANs — an untagged frame lands in a different VLAN on arrival.
failure.tagged-frame-on-access: A tagged frame hit an access port — access ports do not read tags, so the frame is dropped.
failure.port-shutdown: The cable is plugged in, but a port along the way is administratively shut down.
failure.acl-denied: An access list on a router port denied this packet.

lab.deniedByRule: Caught by line {seq} of access list {list}, applied {direction} on port {port} of {device}.
lab.deniedByImplicit: No line of access list {list} matched — the invisible deny at the end of the list caught it (port {port} of {device}, direction {direction}).

diagnosis.device-isolated: A device isn't plugged into anything.
diagnosis.missing-ip: A machine has no IP address set.
diagnosis.missing-gateway: A machine needs to talk outside its own range but has no gateway.
diagnosis.gateway-not-in-subnet: The gateway isn't in the same range as the machine's address.
diagnosis.duplicate-ip: Two devices carry the same IP address.
diagnosis.vlan-mismatch-on-link: A cable joins two ports that sit in different VLANs.
diagnosis.same-subnet-different-vlan: Two machines share an address range but sit in different VLANs.
diagnosis.l2-loop: The diagram has a loop between switches.
diagnosis.trunk-one-side-only: One end of a link is configured as a trunk while the other end is still an access port.
diagnosis.native-vlan-mismatch-on-trunk: The two ends of a trunk declare different native VLANs.
diagnosis.port-shutdown: A port has a cable plugged in but is administratively shut down.

refusal.not-allowed: This task doesn't let you change that — try another angle.
refusal.max-devices: The bench already has all the devices this task needs.
refusal.duplicate-device-id: A device with that name is already on the bench.
refusal.unknown-device: That device could not be found.
refusal.unknown-port: That port could not be found.
refusal.unknown-link: That cable could not be found.
refusal.wrong-device-kind: This device doesn't have that setting.
refusal.port-occupied: This port already has a cable — remove the old one first.
refusal.self-link: A cable needs to join two different devices.
refusal.invalid-vlan: A VLAN number must be between 1 and 4094.
refusal.invalid-ip: An IP address looks like four groups of digits, e.g. 192.168.1.10.
refusal.invalid-prefix: The prefix must be between 0 and 32.
refusal.invalid-priority: A switch priority must be a multiple of 4096, between 0 and 61440.

lab.narrowTitle: The lab wants a wider screen
lab.narrowBody: Everything still works through the configuration panel below — only the diagram gets smaller.
lab.stpNoBlocked: No port has to stay down.
lab.examGoalsNote: Exams do not grade live: this list is the ASSIGNMENT. To see whether the network works, press Try send — it is free.

flow.harderNote: You're on a roll — try typing the answer for this one instead of picking.
flow.supportTitle: Let's pick up a few foundation bricks first
flow.supportBody: The last stretch was bumpy — that's perfectly normal. We'll glance back at a few concepts this lesson stands on: try to recall before you flip, then climb right on.

palace.tourCompleted: You've walked this stretch — in a moment we'll walk it again from memory.
palace.cueAria: The memory image of this room
palace.walkPrompt: You're standing at this door. What's inside?
palace.missingRooms: Couldn't load the building for this walk.
palace.tourGate: Walk this stretch to the end and we'll move on — in a moment you'll walk it again from memory.

clinic.title: Clinic
clinic.lockedBody: Behind this door are real "patients": unplugged cables, a silent DNS, a gateway with the wrong address… You'll play the diagnostician — but the foundation modules come first. Keep learning; the clinic opens itself when you're ready.
clinic.seatLine: You're sitting at the patient's machine {host}. No diagram yet — every clue comes from the terminal below, just like a real on-call shift.
clinic.terminalIntro: Type commands to examine the patient — start with help if you're unsure. Examining is always free.
clinic.terminalPlaceholder: Type a command… (help lists them all)
clinic.termUnknown: This machine has no "{cmd}" command — type help to see the list.
clinic.termCaptureEmpty: No packets captured yet — run ping or tracert first, then capture will have a story to tell.

cmd.ipconfig: show this machine's IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DNS
cmd.ping: send probe packets to an address or name — ping <target>
cmd.tracert: show the router-by-router path to a target — tracert <target>
cmd.nslookup: ask DNS what address a name points to — nslookup <name>
cmd.netstat: list the network connections open on this machine
cmd.arp: show the IP-to-MAC table (ARP cache) this machine has resolved
cmd.capture: show the packet capture of the latest ping/tracert (a tiny Wireshark)
cmd.gpresult: list the Group Policy Objects applied to this machine

clinic.diagnosisHint: Examine through the terminal first — name the illness, then you get to fix it.
clinic.fixIntroEdit: Your turn now: here is the patient's diagram — fix it directly.
clinic.fixIntroBoth: This case has TWO halves: one sits inside the network diagram (fix it by hand below), the other is out of the diagram’s reach (pick an action at the end). Leave either half undone and the machine still is not usable.
clinic.symptomHalfOnly: That is only the network half — the part outside the diagram is still waiting for you.
clinic.actionTitleOutside: The half outside the diagram: how do you handle it?
clinic.fixIntroAction: This illness can't be fixed from where you sit — pick the best course of action.
clinic.symptomStillSick: The patient still shows the original symptom — not cured yet.
clinic.symptomCleared: The original symptom is gone — submit when you're confident.
clinic.listIntro: Every patient you met in Module 11 stays admitted here — re-examine them as often as you like, with the same 3-tier hint ladder.
clinic.listXpNote: XP is awarded only for the first cure of each case
clinic.firstSolveXp: +{xp} XP — this case is now in your casebook.
clinic.resolveNoXp: You've already cured this one — no XP this time, but the practice counts.
clinic.deviceConsolePick: Plug the console into a device
clinic.deviceConsoleIntro: The exam seat can inspect device configs: enable, then run show commands (type ? to see the toolkit). Fixing the network belongs to the repair phase.
clinic.deviceReadOnly: This console is for READING during the exam: only enable/exit/end and show commands run here. To change the network, lock in a diagnosis and use the repair phase.

ps.terminalIntro: Type commands to work the task — Get-Help lists the toolbox if you forget. Trying is always free.
ps.terminalPlaceholder: Type a PowerShell command… (Get-Help lists them)
ps.termUnknown: This machine has no "{cmd}" cmdlet — type Get-Help to see the list.

cmd.Get-NetIPAddress: show the IP addresses of this machine's network cards
cmd.Test-NetConnection: test ping or a TCP port to a target — Test-NetConnection <target> [-Port <n>]
cmd.New-ADUser: create a new user — -Name, -SamAccountName, -Path; or accept bulk rows from the pipe
cmd.Get-ADGroup: look up domain groups — -Identity <group name> or -Filter *
cmd.Get-ADGroupMember: see who a group contains (users or other groups) — -Identity <group name>
cmd.Add-ADGroupMember: add members to a group — -Identity <group name> -Members <sam or group name>
cmd.Import-Csv: read a CSV file into records — pipeable
cmd.Get-Content: read a file line by line
cmd.Select-String: filter lines containing a phrase — Select-String <phrase> [<file>]

ps.termCreatedSilent: (the command finished silently, just like real PowerShell — created {count} user(s); run Get-ADUser to see for yourself)
ps.termAddedSilent: (the command finished silently, just like real PowerShell — run Get-ADGroupMember to see who the group contains now)
ps.goalAdUserCount: The {ou} OU must have at least {atLeast} users
ps.goalGroupMember: User "{sam}" must be a member of {group} (nested groups count)
ps.goalFoundLine: Pulled out a log line containing "{text}"
ps.freeNote: Typing and starting over are free — only "Submit" counts as an attempt.
ps.examGoalsNote: Exams do not grade live: this list is the ASSIGNMENT. To see whether a command worked, verify with Get-* — it is free.

cli.terminalIntro: Type a command and press Enter. Type ? to list the commands this device knows.
cli.termUnknown: The device does not know the command "{cmd}". Type ? to list what it does know.
cli.consoleHint: Pick a device to move the console cable there. On a new device you have to enable again.
cli.freeNote: Typing and starting over are free — only "Submit" counts as an attempt.
cli.goalPortAccess: Port {port} on {device} must be an access port
cli.goalPortTrunk: Port {port} on {device} must be a trunk
cli.goalAccessVlan: Port {port} on {device} must sit in VLAN {vlan}
cli.goalNativeVlan: Trunk {port} on {device} must declare native VLAN {vlan}
cli.goalPortIp: Port {port} on {device} must carry the address {ip}/{prefix}
cli.goalStaticRoute: {device} must have a static route to {destination}/{prefix} via {nextHop}

cmd.enable: enter privileged mode (the prompt turns from > into #)
cmd.interface: pick a port to configure — interface <port name>
cmd.end: jump straight back to privileged mode
cmd.show vlan brief: the VLAN table and which ports sit in which VLAN
cmd.show mac address-table: the MAC addresses the switch has learned
cmd.show interfaces trunk: which ports are trunks, what they carry, and their native VLAN
cmd.show ip interface brief: address and status of every port
cmd.show spanning-tree: who the root is and which port is sitting still
cmd.show access-lists: the access lists and how many packets matched each line
cmd.show ip ospf neighbor: the OSPF neighbor table — who is adjacent, who is not, and why
cmd.show running-config: the whole running configuration (needs enable first)
cmd.vlan: add a VLAN to the switch — vlan <number>
cmd.switchport mode: set the port role — switchport mode access | trunk
cmd.switchport access vlan: put an access port in a VLAN — switchport access vlan <number>
cmd.switchport trunk allowed vlan: VLANs allowed on the trunk — takes 10,20 or 10-12 or all
cmd.switchport trunk native vlan: the untagged VLAN on a trunk — switchport trunk native vlan <number>
cmd.ip address: set a router port's address — ip address <ip> <subnet mask>
cmd.ip route: add a static route — ip route <network> <subnet mask> <next hop>
cmd.router ospf: start an OSPF routing process — router ospf <id>
cmd.network: declare a network for OSPF — network <network> <wildcard> area 0
cmd.access-list: write one filter rule — access-list <n> permit|deny <protocol> <source> <destination>
cmd.ip access-group: apply a filter list to the port — ip access-group <n> in|out
cmd.shutdown: shut the port down by command
cmd.no shutdown: bring a shut port back up

cli.examGoalsNote: Exams do not grade live: this list is the ASSIGNMENT. To see whether the config took, verify with show commands — they are free.
cli.goalNativeMatch: Both trunk ends ({portA} on {deviceA} and {portB} on {deviceB}) must declare the SAME native VLAN

grad.subtitleNhapMon: You started this course from zero — now home networks, DNS, NAT, AD and an on-call shift are no longer strangers. Below are your own numbers.
grad.subtitleTrungCap: From your first ARP shout to a branch office built with your own hands — twenty-one modules, one full circle. This is the mirror of the whole road.
grad.mapAria: Map of all course modules; filled cells are modules you have passed
grad.journeyLine: From your first lesson on {from} to the last one on {to} — with {active} days when you actually sat down to study. The gaps in between are not holes: memory only holds when it is given distance.
grad.certBody: Download a PNG that copies the numbers above — for your files, to send to someone, or just to keep. Nothing is sent anywhere: the image is drawn on your own machine.
grad.certIntro: has completed {passed}/{total} modules of this computer networking course, including hands-on work in the lab, the device console and the fault clinic.
grad.certError: The image could not be produced right now. Try once more, or open this page in another browser.
grad.nextRoadNhapMon: The intermediate road is open on the Learn page: VLSM, trunks, OSPF, ACLs — and a branch office waiting to be built by your own hands at the end.
grad.nextRoadTrungCap: The course is complete, but the Review box opens every day — memory pays in installments, and those cards will keep visiting you.
grad.noXpNote: This screen awards no XP — it is a mirror, not a reward. Your score lives in what stayed in your hands.
grad.notReachedTitle: This milestone is not open yet
grad.notReachedBody: Passing the final module test of the stage opens this screen — the map on the Learn page shows where you stand.
grad.chuaSoatDuocTitle: Can't check the whole journey yet
grad.chuaSoatDuocBody: This screen recounts the entire course and issues your certificate, but {count} topics haven't downloaded yet — checking a partial course would print a wrong number onto a document you keep for good. Download the rest and come back; nothing is lost.

dispute.action: I think my answer is right
dispute.thanks: Your exact wording has been saved for the author to re-check the answer list. This question still counts as unsolved — give it one more try.

weakDrill.title: Practice your shaky questions
weakDrill.correctAgain: Straight out this time — that old slip is healing.
weakDrill.openLesson: Reopen the lesson that teaches this
weakDrill.doneBody: You got {correct}/{total} of your shaky questions right. For anything still wobbly, reopen the lesson — this is not about points, it is so the next encounter costs you no thinking.
weakDrill.noXpNote: No XP and no change to your review schedule: you already solved these once.
weakDrill.chuaLotHoi: Read the solution and it still won't go in?
weakDrill.chuaLotDaGhi: Noted — whoever writes the lessons will read this. The full list lives on your Profile page.
weakDrill.quenDoneBody: You got {correct}/{total} right around the things you keep forgetting. Anything still shaky is worth reopening the lesson for — what slips again and again is usually what never found something to hold on to, not what you studied too little.
weakDrill.quenEmptyBody: This list comes from things you have forgotten twice or more. Nothing here means nothing has slipped that far — keep reviewing.
weakDrill.emptyBody: Questions you had to retry gather here on their own. An empty list means you are moving smoothly — keep learning.

profile.title: Profile
profile.emptyBadges: Badges are coming in a later version — your XP, streak and every case you cure are all being recorded.
profile.weakIntro: Not a score — these are the questions you had to retry the most, which makes them the best places to revisit.
profile.analysisHeadline: You stumble most on {kind} — on {pct}% of those questions ({attempted} answered). Not a verdict on you: that type simply wants more reps.
profile.analysisNotEnough: So far you have stumbled on {stumbled} of {attempted} answered questions — not enough to say what kind of slip it is. Come back after a few more lessons, when the numbers can tell the truth.
profile.analysisTotals: Totals: {stumbled}/{attempted} questions stumbled on · {fails} incorrect attempts · {solutions} needed the solution.
profile.analysisDrillNote: No XP here — this is the practice room, not the arena.
profile.quangTitle: Your longest unbroken sitting this week: {phut} minutes.
profile.quangDai: At that length, what you learn later starts writing over what came before — 25-30 minutes then a few minutes up on your feet sticks better.
profile.thangIntro: The same question types, measured against the mark the app kept on {ngay}. This is your stumble rate counted from the start of the course, so it moves slowly — a small move is a long way.
profile.thangCho: The app has just kept this month's mark. From next month, this is where you'll see which question types you've improved on.
profile.thangRowAria: {kind}: stumble rate went from {truoc}% to {nay}% across {attempted} questions done
profile.disputeIntro: The times you tapped "I think my answer is right". Your exact wording is kept so the author can re-check the accepted answers — an answer list that is too narrow is the question's fault, not yours.
profile.disputeFromTest: This one came from a module test
profile.memoryIntro: Each bar fades along your own review schedule: solid right after a review, pale by the day you must recall it. Pale is not lost — it is an appointment, and recalling something just as it fades is what makes it stick deepest.
profile.rhythmNghiHet: No sessions in the last eight weeks — that is fine, a broken rhythm can be picked back up. One short session gives this week its first bar.
profile.rhythmIntro: This is your own baseline — the idea Module 20 teaches: you can only spot an unusual week once you know your usual one. A short bar is not a reproach, just a busy week.
profile.freezeNote: Missing a day won't break your streak — you get 2 automatic "freezes" each month.
profile.backupBody: Progress lives in this device's browser — clearing browsing data or switching machines loses it. Export a file now and then; import it on a new machine to pick up where you left off.
profile.backupImportConfirm: Importing will REPLACE all progress on this device with the file's progress. The current state is copied first, so picking the wrong file can still be undone. Continue?
profile.backupImportBad: That file is not a valid NetMaster backup — double-check you picked the right one.
profile.backupImportNewer: This backup comes from a newer version of the app — update the app, then import again.
profile.anhChupBody: Every day you open the app to study, it quietly keeps a copy of your progress; it also keeps one right before any big overwrite — a data upgrade, or importing a backup file. The 3 most recent are kept, so if something looks wrong you can roll straight back.
profile.anhChupEmpty: No copies yet — the first one is kept next time you open the app.
profile.anhChupConfirm: Roll progress back to the copy from {luc}? Anything learned after that point is lost. The current state is copied first, so a mis-click can still be undone.
profile.hayQuenIntro: Different from "where you stumble" below: stumbling happens while you're still learning a lesson, whereas these are things you already finished, felt sure of, and lost again days later. Forgetting once is just how memory works, so it doesn't count; twice or more lands here — a sign the current explanation lands but doesn't stick.
profile.hayQuenEmpty: Nothing has slipped away twice yet. This list fills itself in as you review — empty means you're doing fine, not that the app isn't counting.
profile.chuaLotIntro: This is YOUR word about the teaching, not a score. Every other number in the app measures how far you got; only this one separates "haven't studied enough" from "studied it and the explanation never landed" — and only you can tell. Hand this list to whoever writes the lessons and they know what to rewrite.
profile.anhChupLyDoNhap: kept before the last file import
profile.aoGiacIntro: Cards you felt sure about and then could not recall. Recognising something on a reread is not the same as remembering it — this is exactly where memory fools you.

nhacNghi.title: Time for a short break
nhacNghi.body: You've studied {phut} minutes straight. Your brain needs a few quiet minutes to file what you just learned — walk around, then come back; it will stick better.
